scene_description: A small light-walled office with a blind above a low wooden cubby shelf, a floor lamp, two rolling chairs, a desk, a paneled door, and a large potted grass-like plant.
initial_target_observations: Both initial chairs have curved pale shells and visible dark central pedestals with wheeled bases. The nearer chair's shell appears connected to the central support; the farther chair's connection is partly obscured by the desk and shell. The reference also shows pedestal-supported chairs, with darker gray shells and differently oriented seats.
candidate_target_observations: The candidate's central chair retains a visible dark pedestal and wheeled base beneath its curved shell. The right chair's lower support is mostly hidden by the foreground desk, although a dark base fragment is visible. The candidate's chair shells are lighter and more upright-looking than in the reference.
geometric_plausibility_observations: The central chair has a visually plausible shell-to-pedestal arrangement and radiating wheeled base, but RGB does not establish actual mesh contact. The second chair's connection is occluded. The shelf, lamp, door, and desk have recognizable simplified geometry. The reference door is dark and shown at an angle, whereas the candidate door is light gray and appears more flush to the wall.
new_visible_defects: The candidate viewpoint leaves the right chair's support much less visible behind the large foreground desk; this is an occlusion, not proof of missing geometry. The lamp shade overlaps the left portion of the blind in the candidate view.
other_changes: Compared with the initial image, the candidate is viewed from a different angle: the desk moves visually to the lower right, the plant is cropped at the right edge, and the door is nearer the center. This produces both closer and less comparable spatial relationships to the reference. Both reconstructions use flatter, paler materials and more uniform lighting than the reference, lacking its pronounced wood grain, darker door, and stronger surface variation. Black corner marks on the blind are conspicuous in both reconstructions.

evidence.description: A gray chair shell sits above a dark central pedestal and wheeled base.
The nearer chair shows a curved shell, central support and wheeled base.
The central chair has a visible pedestal and wheeled base beneath its shell.
The right chair is partially hidden by the desk, including most of its support.
A dark paneled door stands at an angle against the light wall.
A lighter gray paneled door appears closer to the wall plane.
The blind has dark corner marks and is overlapped by the lamp shade.

uncertainty: No specific target defect is identified, so chair support is assessed as the most relevant visible feature. Different viewpoints and foreground occlusion prevent a reliable determination of whether support geometry changed or improved. A single RGB view cannot establish mesh contact, hidden geometry, collision, or learned capability.
